messages:
maya (partnerships): quick heads-up — partner 'VertexCloud' pinged us: marketplace image that includes our runtime + driver is failing a subset of inference jobs after the recent runtime bump. They saw GPU hangs and OOMs. Can eng-runtime / SRE weigh in on a coordination plan for driver/CUDA/ROCm version pinning + hotfix cadence?

alex (eng-runtime): thanks for flagging. do we have logs from VertexCloud? usually these are either driver/kernel mismatches or newer CUDA ABI changes.

maya (partnerships): yes attached in their message — pasted snippet below: 
```
[ERR] CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED at step 34
GPU 0: process stuck, stack traces show kernel timeout
nvidia-smi shows driver 535.54 but container expects 535.86
```
They said marketplace image was built with our 0.9.7 runtime image.

cheng (eng-ml): hmm 0.9.7 included a kernel optimization that changes shared memory layout for some fused kernels — we've validated on driver 535.86+ but not 535.54. That mismatch could cause crashes.

ramesh (nvidia-rep): from NV side: driver 535.54 -> 535.86 had a small CUDA runtime ABI tweak affecting cublasLt for large workspaces. We'll confirm the back-compat, but best practice is to pin driver major+minor. We recommend pairing: runtime build validated with driver 535.86.

alex (eng-runtime): actionable proposal: 1) publish a compatibility matrix we sign-off with partners listing validated driver/CUDA/ROCm combos; 2) add runtime image tags that explicitly encode validated driver (eg: redwood/runtime:0.9.7-driver-535.86); 3) recommend marketplace sellers use those explicit tags and block autoswitching drivers on their host images.

maya (partnerships): +1. partners will need messaging for marketplace guidelines and a short checklist.

dana (eng-sre): operational constraints: some cloud hosts auto-update host drivers via repo packages. We'll need two things: a startup-time sanity probe to detect incompatible host driver vs container expectations, and a fallback policy (auto-restart into a degraded CPU-only fallback or surface actionable error). Can the runtime add a probe?

alex (eng-runtime): yes — we can add a probe that calls cudaDriverGetVersion() at startup and compares to expected pinned version. If mismatch, runtime will either: a) refuse to start (fail fast), or b) enter degraded mode (CPU path) if allowed by customer policy. Which do you want as default?

sarah (product): default should be fail-fast for marketplace images — sellers need deterministic behavior. For Dedicated/private deployments, make the degraded mode opt-in. We'll draft default policies in the partner playbook.

ramesh (nvidia-rep): to help here, NV can publish driver bundles for marketplace images with explicit driver SKUs. Also can provide a hotfix channel for critical regressions. If you give us the failing repro we can prioritize a micro-release.

alex (eng-runtime): next steps from eng-runtime side: a) add runtime startup probe + log message; b) produce image tags that include driver pin; c) update release checklist to include driver compatibility smoke tests (GPU hangs, cublas sanity, mem checks). I'll open a short PR for (a) and (b) today.

cheng (eng-ml): also adding to the test harness: run our perf/regression suite with older drivers (535.54) and newer (535.86) + ROCm matrix (5.4/5.6) on CI. We should detect perf regressions and OOM patterns before release.

deploy-bot: deploy request created by alex for branch fix/driver-probe — ID: DRV-4319 — canary to staging cluster queued.

dana (eng-sre): I'll coordinate with VertexCloud ops to request a repro image and hold their marketplace publish until we confirm which runtime tag to use. Also will add a HostDriverPolicy doc entry to prevent auto-updates for marketplace-certified VMs.

maya (partnerships): thanks all. I'll draft a short partner-facing note: 1) use runtime images with explicit driver tag; 2) verify host driver versions per compatibility matrix; 3) contact NV support channel for driver hotfixes. Will loop in legal/marketing for marketplace announcement wording.

alex (eng-runtime): one extra detail — for ROCm (AMD) we need the same approach: pin ROCm kernel/driver combos (e.g., ROCm 5.6 + kernel-5.15 patches). Cheng, can you smoke-test AMDFire variants?

cheng (eng-ml): yes, I'll schedule ROCm runs. We should also document fallback for ROCm (no degraded CPU path for now).

ramesh (nvidia-rep): I'll open a partner ticket with driver bundles and a short FAQ we can co-brand. Also will share our internal regression tracker so we can correlate.

maya (partnerships): perfect. Can we have an initial compatibility matrix + partner checklist draft by EOD tomorrow? Partners are asking for it for their marketplace submission windows.

alex (eng-runtime): aiming for a draft this afternoon. Will update DRV-4319 with artifacts and a sample image tag pattern.

maya (partnerships): thanks — I'll ping VertexCloud and hold their publish. :thumbsup:

sarah (product): note for roadmap — include "driver compatibility" as a checkbox for Dedicated readiness gating. We'll sync in next week's partner ops sync.

maya (partnerships): will do. closing the loop here. If anyone gets a repro or hotfix from NV, paste it here so partnerships can coordinate announcement timing. :slightly_smiling_face:
